title: Normalized ordinary derived scalar adjunctions
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $d$ an adic coefficient datum [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], $B$ normalized strict scalar balancing, $f:U\to V$ a scheme morphism, and $P$ a normalized $\mathrm{PullCompatibility}$ for $B$ [lem-weil-pbc-strict-quotient-scalar-balancing]. Write $L^a:D(A_V)\to D(A_U)$ and $L^0:D(\underline A_V)\to D(\underline A_U)$ for the two ordinary unbounded derived pullbacks supplied by $P$, $r_U,r_V$ for scalar restriction, and $a:L^ar_U\cong r_VL^0$ for $P.a$, with functor composition written in execution order. There exist right adjoints $R^a$ and $R^0$ and adjunctions $L^a\dashv R^a$ and $L^0\dashv R^0$, together with a natural isomorphism $\chi:R^ar_V\cong r_UR^0$ whose forward transformation is exactly the adjunction mate of $a^{-1}$. No completeness, boundedness, constructibility or properness assumption is imposed.

proof.text: Construct the two module adjunctions from the published small pro-etale geometric adjunction and coefficient identifications. The normalized ordinaryScalar identifies their underlying pullbacks; conservative exact scalar restriction implies exactness of completed pullback. On the underlying additive sheaves the ordinary mate is the canonical identity, and hence is invertible.

proof.text: The module categories are Grothendieck and have K-injective resolutions. Localize the exact pullback and derive its right adjoint on K-injectives. Derived adjunction constructs the unbounded adjunctions. Their transpose equations are computed on complexes by the ordinary module transpose and derived comparison maps.

proof.text: Flat scalar restriction preserves K-injectives. Extend P.a_computes from its flat-term K-flat resolving class to all complexes by naturality and flat resolutions. Compute the derived mate on a K-injective target using the ordinary counit: after the invertible derived direct-image comparison maps, it is the invertible ordinary mate. K-injective resolutions extend invertibility to every target. Choose chi as this mate isomorphism.

lean.statement:
theorem strictScalarOrdinaryAdjointsExist (d : AdicCoefficientDatum A) (B : Balancing d)
    {U V : Scheme.{u}} (f : U ⟶ V)
    (P : PullCompatibility f d (B.ρ V) (B.ρ U)) :
    ∃ (rightA : D (ring U d true) ⥤ D (ring V d true))
      (right0 : D (ring U d false) ⥤ D (ring V d false))
      (adjA : P.completed.ordinary ⊣ rightA)
      (adj0 : P.constant.ordinary ⊣ right0)
      (χ : rightA ⋙ dres (scalar V d) ≅ dres (scalar U d) ⋙ right0),
      χ.hom = (mateEquiv adjA adj0 (TwoSquare.mk _ _ _ _ P.a.inv)).natTrans
